skill.name: research-agent-optimization
skill.description: Guides improvements to a research agent by reducing duplicate API calls, handling quota limits, fixing web search tools, and improving streamed source output.
skill.summary: Improve research agent reliability, search integration, streaming progress, and source rendering.
skill.author: BenderFendor

security_audit.summary: All static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown inline code, project file references, and prose checklist items. No executable command invocation, prompt injection attempt, data exfiltration intent, or system reconnaissance behavior was found in SKILL.md.

static_findings.snippet: - Add optional `--skip-gemini-analysis` mode for article analysis when quota is low
- Set model to `gemini-2.0-flash` (faster, lower token cost) instead of `gemini-2.0-flash-exp`
- Verify DuckDuckGo import: `from duckduckgo_search import DDGS` (not `ddgs` or `DuckDuckGo`)
- Ensure `web_search` and `news_search` tools are properly bound to LLM
- Use `exa-code` to verify current DuckDuckGo API patterns
- Expand SSE event types: `tool_start` includes tool name + query parameters
- [ ] Implement request cache in `search_internal_news` with 5min TTL
- [ ] Update `research_stream()` to emit granular tool start/result events
- Add caching layer for semantic search results (avoid duplicate queries within 5min window)
- Submit invalid query and verify doesn't crash

content.value_statement: Research agents can waste API quota, fail web searches, and show unclear progress. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a focused plan to improve reliability and source presentation.
actual_capabilities: Identifies backend and frontend files related to research agent behavior.
Outlines caching, batching, and retry changes for lower API usage.
Specifies DuckDuckGo tool initialization checks and fallback behavior.
Defines clearer streaming events for tool starts, results, and idle status.
Guides source card rendering instead of raw JSON response blocks.
Lists checks for quota handling, search results, rendering, and errors.
limitations: It is an implementation guide, not an executable automation script.
It assumes the target project has the named backend and frontend files.
It does not provide complete code patches or test files.
It depends on current APIs for Gemini and DuckDuckGo search libraries.

use_cases.title: Stabilize Research Agent Backends
use_cases.description: Backend engineers can use the workflow to reduce duplicate searches and handle quota failures cleanly.

use_cases.title: Improve Research UI Feedback
use_cases.description: Frontend developers can map streaming events into clear progress messages and source card displays.

use_cases.title: Plan Agent Reliability Work
use_cases.description: Technical leads can turn the checklist into scoped work for search, streaming, and error handling.

prompt_templates.title: Review Current Agent Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review the current research agent flow. Summarize which files control search, streaming, errors, and source rendering.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Quota Improvements
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to create an implementation plan for batching, caching, retry backoff, and quota warning behavior in the research agent.

prompt_templates.title: Fix Search Tool Integration
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate debugging for web search failures.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to inspect DuckDuckGo search setup and tool binding. Recommend targeted changes and checks for reliable web and news search.

prompt_templates.title: Implement End-to-End Streaming UX
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced implementation across backend and frontend.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to implement granular streaming events, user-facing status messages, source cards, error states, and verification checks.

output_examples.input: Improve quota handling for the research agent.
output: A prioritized plan for cache, batching, retry backoff, and quota warnings.
A list of affected backend files and verification checks.
User-facing error messages for rate limits and timeouts.

output_examples.input: Make streaming progress clearer during research.
output: A proposed event model for tool start, result, idle, and error updates.
Plain-language status messages for web, news, internal, and article fetch tools.
Frontend rendering checks for progress messages and source cards.

output_examples.input: Fix raw JSON showing in research answers.
output: Guidance to keep final answers as plain text.
A separate Sources section grouped by retrieval method.
Checks for duplicate source removal and article modal behavior.

best_practices: Start by tracing the full request path before changing retries or streaming events.
Add caching and batching with clear cache keys, expiry rules, and duplicate source handling.
Verify user-visible errors and logs without exposing stack traces or sensitive values.
anti_patterns: Adding automatic retries without backoff or quota awareness.
Mixing source metadata into the final answer as raw JSON.
Showing generic progress messages when specific tool activity is available.

faq.question: Does this skill execute code automatically?
faq.answer: No. It is a written workflow for an agent to follow while editing a project.

faq.question: Which systems does it target?
faq.answer: It targets a research agent with Gemini calls, DuckDuckGo search, SSE streaming, and a frontend search page.

faq.question: Can it help reduce API quota usage?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends batching, caching, duplicate query avoidance, and lower cost model selection.

faq.question: Does it cover source attribution?
faq.answer: Yes. It asks the agent to render source cards and remove raw JSON blocks from answers.

faq.question: Is it limited to Claude?
faq.answer: No. The marketplace metadata supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What should users verify after changes?
faq.answer: Users should verify cache behavior, web search results, streaming events, source cards, and error scenarios.
